utterances.text: There were questions about whether you had said that Muslim civilians were leaving Fakovici with wheat bags or somewhere else and you referred to Zanjevo. Is Zanjevo part of Fakovici or is it part of some other village?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim villages that are bigger than Fakovici is Zanjevo, Abdulici, that's right next to that village. Zanjevo is an ethnically pure Muslim village, and it's larger than the Serbian village of Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. But it's part of Fakovici; correct? The broader area of Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how that municipality is organised. That's the Bratunac municipality. I corrected myself. I didn't say that they went from Fakovici but from the Muslim village of Zanjevo. That's where they were carrying the sacks from. I don't know. I assume that the Serbs organised the local communes in such a way that that would be the Fakovici local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And the final question in relation to D469, an exhibit which you were shown and you were asked about whether it was a dawn attack in Kravica. My question is simply this: Aside from what your group was doing in the direction in which you were travelling, do you know what was happening in the whole broad area of Kravica? Do you know when any actions or combat occurred in the whole area of Kravica? Or do you simply know what your group was doing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On that particular day, that is, the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 7th of January, all I knew is what my group was doing on the Avdagina Njive-Kajici-Kravica direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jones. Judge Brydensholt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Yes. When this Kadir Hamidovic arrived, how long do you think he has been under his way from Glogova? Do you have any idea? Did he tell you anything of that?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell us anything. Maybe -- I don't know if he walked to Srebrenica, four or five hours, or two or three hours by truck to Osmace and then another hour to actually reach Osmace. So he needed at least seven or eight hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: You mentioned again the possibility that he got a lift on a truck. Were there at all truck traffic on that road, that means Muslim truck traffic?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was very rare. Perhaps a tractor would pass by on the road. I'm talking about January or before January. People did as best they could. They took fuel from the electrical power stations. There was a shortage of fuel so these vehicles were not used very often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: When your group then decided to go to Kravica, how were you transferred there?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we walked to the asphalt road and then we took a lorry to Srebrenica. From Srebrenica we walked to -- I don't know exactly which villages, Milacevici, Pale, Avdagina Njive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: So again there were lorry to transfer you to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: How -- how could you explain that there was a lorry there? Was that just by chance or was that something you had agreed with somebody that it should be there? You were a big group, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our village, it's a rich village with a lot of tractors, trucks, these were private trucks, two or three, and a lot of tractors. I'm talking about five or six. But there was no fuel. I don't know how they managed to get some fuel, but we took the truck from our village to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Well, when you came to Kravica and the attack started, did you notice any trenches?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We noticed Serb trenches, which they had their own trenches on the approaches to Glogova and Avdagina Njive but our people didn't have them, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Were those trenches manned when you attacked?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on the 7th. They were celebrating, as I said, and on the right side, there was four-barrel Flak which, at that point in time, as they were celebrating, was covering the entire area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: During the afternoon at around 4.00, you got a message, I understand, that Kragljivoda was under attack. How did you get that message?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Somebody from the group, probably as a joke or, I don't know for what reason, said that Kragljivoda was attacked, and we went back at about 4.00. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you mean to say -- I want to make sure that the interpretation is correct because it says, I don't know exactly. Somebody from the group, probably as a joke or, I don't know for what reason, said that Kragljivoda was attacked, and we went back at about 4.00. I don't know. I mean, would you -- would you have reacted and organised a group and went to help upon a joke? Or a possible joke? I mean, I don't think these were matters that called for a possible joke, you know.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just say this: The main information was conveyed orally. There was no means of communications. No communication devices existed in my group throughout that time -- we are talking about until March. Meaning that we understood that as correct information and we went back. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. We received that information that Kragljivoda was attacked, and we returned at about 4.00. I'm talking about my group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a follow-up question to this Kravica event. Now you gave testimony that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, before you proceed, I want to make sure it's okay with the interpreters and the technicians and the rest of the staff that we go beyond our time for a few minutes. I see okay from the left-hand side and okay from the right-hand side. I take it that there are no objections. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, you had testified that you have been in Kravica with a group of about 50 people. Then you told us we have been informed to go back and who decided that you would go back?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dudic, Mirsad was with us in our group, and he said, Let's go, we will return to Osmace, or actually go up there towards Kragljivoda because Kragljivoda was attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So he decided to -- that you would go back and all the people followed this decision?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, this was a decision in former instances you always would deny that there was a decision, and I had the impression that, for instance, with regard to distribution of ammunition, that you would not call a decision if it was taken spontaneous. Is that a correct interpretation of your image, or what you mean with decision? Or would you agree that a decision can also be spontaneous?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To clear this up, spontaneous versus decision, this was an area that was 50 to 60 kilometres away from Osmace. Hence, we had to go back on foot. We went on foot as far as Srebrenica, and then by a truck. So whoever was left behind the group had to go on foot for days, and it was cold. So they obeyed for that reason, and I reiterate that everything was voluntary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: That wasn't actually my point. I only wanted to make sure that even a decision can be made on the spot, but somebody has to say that because this way or we go that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Make it to him as a proposition. Would you agree that a decision can also be a spontaneous -- can be spontaneously taken? Just answer yes or no. I mean, it's a plain question.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, spontaneous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, on your way to Kravica, you told us that "there were about 50 lads in my group." This is on page 1078 -- 10718 in the transcript. You said: "And during the night we were joined by the lads from Miholjevine, Mosici, Delici led by Mefail, nickname Zis." And you would say: "And they came to the area independently of us." Now, what does it mean, "independently of us"? What do you mean by independently?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Independently? Well, that word means that we were not in our group and we saw them for the first time between the 6th and the 7th. So they didn't come with our group. I don't know how they came there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You said "independently of us." So would it be possible or do you know whether the others from Miholjevina, Mosici, Delici came together?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to distinguishing civilians and fighters, you had told us in connection with Fakovici, that is on page 10680 -- 106 -- "Most of the people from my group had weapons but we had no coordination, no links with our civilians. We were interested in them and they were not interested -- we were not interested in them and they were not interested in us." Now, how did you -- could you distinguish civilians from fighters?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't. Only by weapons. By people within armed groups who had a rifle. Otherwise there was no difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You told us in another connection that among your group you had those who had weapons and others who had no weapons.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So there was no distinction. Everyone was wearing, say, a civilian shirt, pants, trousers, a jacket, and there was no distinction. Only if someone had a rifle that meant that he was counted within the group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, if I could -- could I conclude, when you said "we were not interested in civilians," that you were not interested in people which did not have weapons? Although they belonged to your group?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what I meant. I said the movement, if I may call them carpet-baggers, that I meant their movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. No further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Judge Eser. I'm not going to put any questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I put -- I hesitate to ask but I have one question. It's just in light of the questions put by Your Honours in reference to a joke. I'd like to clarify, if I can, with one question what that might be about, because I'm not comfortable with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, because it's still there in the transcript and not say that you are never used to it. Go ahead, but please be as short as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Buric, when it comes to your group going from Osmace to Kravica, was it always your intention to go back to Osmace after the action or were you planning to remain there?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We went with the intention to return.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And when you mentioned a joke, and correct me if I've -- if I'm under a misapprehension, but was it something of the nature of someone saying, We better get back or we will be attacked, too, or something like that or was it something else that you had in mind? What sort of a joke was it?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was -- the correct information was that the Serbs launched an attack at Kragljivoda from all artillery weapons. They were doing that regularly. And their aviation participated as well as their artillery. From all positions. I wanted to add something. I felt the need to explain something. Since I worked in the school, I can ask you what has a school done in Srebrenica that it should receive a grenade or a shell or a bomb from a plane? There were refugees in the high school centre and the plane dropped a bomb there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll put the question myself. You mentioned a joke earlier on. You said I don't know, it could have been a joke. I mean, someone could have said it as a joke. What would -- what would the joke sound like? What would this person say as a joke?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to tell you, Your Honour, perhaps I may offer a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please answer the question. Mr. Buric, we are here over the time. Otherwise we will bring you here again tomorrow. I mean, we have to come to an end. You mentioned a joke. You said it possibly could have been a joke. I don't know. That's what you said. What would have been the joke? What would have been the words used as a joke? This is all I want. It's a short sentence, which would be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was no joke. The attack was real. I may have used a wrong word, but the attack against Kragljivoda was underway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones. If you want to ask another question, but that will be the final one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm satisfied with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Buric, that brings to an end your testimony here. Before you are escorted out by our usher and you are assisted to your return home, I wish to thank you on behalf of Judge Brydensholt, Judge Eser and myself but also on behalf of the Tribunal for having been kind enough to come over and give evidence in this trial. Also, on behalf of everyone present here, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And before we quit, you will allow me just a few seconds to thank the interpreters, the technicians and all the members of the Registry and the staff, plus the cooperation of both parties, to have made it possible for this witness to go back according to schedule. I appreciate it all on behalf of the Trial Chamber and on behalf of the Tribunal. We will meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00 with a new witness. Right. Thank you.
